content:
Quick scratchpad notes from 2026-03-10 interview. Notes to self / passback for loop planning.

Candidate: Aisha Khan (resume: distributed-systems+inference infra). Role: Sr Runtime Engineer (inference serving).
Interviewers: Diego (me), Maya (runtime infra), Evelyn (applied ML).

Impression highlights:
- Very comfortable with distributed request routing and policy-based fallbacks (latency vs cost). Had a clear mental model for prioritizing requests across tiers.
- Articulated a useful autoscale policy that included burst capacity + soft limits to protect SLOs — liked the idea of dynamic buffer based on recent p99 token rate.
- Good intuition on KV cache TTLs and when to prefer prefix cache vs full-sequence cache. Suggested hybrid approach for chat workloads.
- On quantization: knows practical tradeoffs (INT8 vs 4-bit), but hasn't implemented custom kernels; relied on existing libs (Torch Inductor / Triton). Not a dealbreaker but flag for later.
- On observability: emphasized token-level tracing, per-model cost at route-level, and hooks for eval rollbacks. Matches Redwood priorities.

Coding exercise notes:
- Prompt: implement a concurrency-safe LRU-like KV cache with TTL and a very small API. Candidate implemented a map+linked list approach, used locks around mutations.
- Pros: clear design, handled TTL cleanup with background sweeper, explained complexity tradeoffs.
- Cons: locking strategy could be improved (coarse-grained lock may block hot-path reads), missed micro-optimizations (read-mostly fast path with atomic ops). Edge-case: race on item eviction while read in progress — candidate acknowledged and sketched fix but didn't implement.
- Tests: basic happy-path tests only. No stress test or contention scenario.

Behavioral / Ops stories:
- On-call story: described incident where model KV cache thrash caused high latency; they debugged by tracing tail latencies and introducing request sampling + backpressure. Good operational instincts.
- Team collaboration: described mentoring juniors, pair debugging sessions. Positive signals for knowledge transfer.

Concerns / follow-ups:
- Depth on kernel-level perf (CUDA/Triton) is lighter. For roles where we expect them to tune kernels directly, add a technical deep-dive or take-home on kernel selection/compilation tradeoffs.
- Concurrency coding polish: prefer to see a follow-up pairing session (live) on implementing lock-free read path or sharded locks.
- Quantization experience: ask specific questions about accuracy regression detection and rehousing quantized models into fallback paths.

Suggested interview plan for final loop:
- 60m SRE deep dive with Marcus: incident postmortem + SLO design for multi-tenant inference. Focus: routing policies, graceful degradation, cost-levers.
- 45m live pairing with a small concurrency challenge (focus on contention, atomic ops, sharding). Evaluate implementable fixes for the coarse lock.
- 30m final sync with product/PM for alignment on customer-facing tradeoffs (latency vs cost) and behavioral fit.

Compensation / leveling note:
- Looks like strong Sr IC (level: Senior or Senior+ depending on kernel expectations). Compensation band: mid to high senior range. If we need kernel-level expertise, consider leveling toward Staff after final loops.

Action items (my notes):
- [ ] Schedule final loop; include Marcus, pairing engineer, product PM
- [ ] Prepare 15-20 minute kernel-level prompt for Marcus if we decide to probe deeper
- [ ] Add a short pre-read: candidate's GitHub links + ask to prepare one on-call incident to discuss in depth
- [ ] Send quick passback to recruiting: strong advance, highlight follow-ups above

Notes-to-self: keep loop tight on concurrency and kernel depth. If kernel depth is shallow but other signals strong, we can hire and pair on kernel work via mentorship and targeted hiring (we're comfortable hiring for serving design + ops if they can learn Triton internals on the job).

Unresolved questions (flag for final loop):
- Has the candidate shipped custom kernels or PRs to Triton/inductor? Linked GH profile missing one clear repo — ask for examples.
- How comfortable are they with quantization QA pipelines and automated regression detection?

End of quick passback.
